question: At the residues the annotation says do the chemistry -- rather than wherever on a structure the largest patch happens to lie -- how many residues can a macrocycle reach, and is there a hydrophobic patch there?
answer: 16 of the 26 units carry at least one annotated site residue inside the coordinates that were folded, and the patch at that location is measured for each. The largest patch of the unit is at the site in 15 of them. 1 units have nothing but proteolytic processing sites in them, so their figures describe a chain terminus; 10 units have no measurable site at all and each says why. Read the confidence first: 53 of the 104 anchors sit below the folding tool's own confident threshold, so for 13 of the 16 measured units at least one residue the site was measured on is a position the model did not commit to. Over the chemistry residues alone -- processing sites dropped, which are chain termini and disordered by construction -- it is 46 of 97 anchors across 10 of the 15 units that carry one, and that is the figure to read beside `chemistry_only`. 15 of the 16 measured units are measured at the residues the annotation names and 1 are not, which is the gate a page must pass a figure through before printing it as this site's. The rows are numbered along 6 reading frames of this genome, named per row, because 26 pairs of them carry spans that overlap as integers while sharing no residue.

numbering.on_the_relative: the homolog's UniProt entry, which is where the annotation lives and the only numbering a curator ever wrote.
numbering.in_this_genome: 1-based along the open reading frame of this genome the chain was located in, through the alignment blocks and never through an offset: the held-out spike S1 chain is +10 at its start and +31 at its end, and nsp12 sits in a different reading frame entirely. Frame-local, so the row's `reading_frame` is part of the number and not a note beside it.
numbering.which_reading_frame: `reading_frame` on every row: the pool index, and beside it the strand, the codon offset and the nucleotide start, which identify the frame without rebuilding this run's pool. Two spans in different frames can overlap as integers and share no residue -- over this run 26 pairs of rows do -- so a join, a sort or a plot on `span_in_this_genome` alone is wrong by construction. `agrees_with_the_folds_record` checks this module's own alignment against the frame the coordinates were cut from.
numbering.in_the_fold: 1..N of the folded coordinates, because ESMFold numbers the sequence it was given from one. This is the numbering to type into a structure viewer, and it is the unit's span start subtracted from the position in this genome, plus one.
numbering.verified_on: the main protease, whose catalytic dyad maps to folded positions 41 and 145, where the coordinate file carries HIS and CYS. Then over everything: all 106 anchors carry the residue the relative's entry has at the annotated position, where shifting every anchor by one residue drops that to 9 of 106 and by two to 5 or 6. The chain of three numberings is checked and not assumed.

how_to_read.before_anything_else: measured_at_the_annotated_residues. True means the anchors this row's figures were measured at carry the residues the annotation names there; False means they do not, and then the figures describe some other location and must not be published as this site's. None means nobody could say -- the relative's entry has no residue at an annotated position, or the coordinates name one outside the twenty `geometry._letter` knows. anchors_at_the_wrong_residue carries both residues and both numberings per anchor, so a constant gap between the numbers reads as a shifted window rather than as several surprises. True on 15 of the 16 measured units here; the deposited lane has a measured case where it is 0 of 12.
how_to_read.first: anchor_confidence.mean_plddt and below_the_confident_threshold. A site measured on residues the model placed at pLDDT 30 is a measurement of noise, and no figure below it means anything without this one. Where chemistry_only.anchor_confidence is present it is the one that governs chemistry_only's figures: the row's block is computed over every anchor including the proteolytic processing sites, which are chain termini and disordered by construction, so it can condemn a measurement for a reason the measurement does not depend on.
how_to_read.positions_in_the_fold: ask 3's list of amino-acid positions, in the numbering the coordinates use. This is what goes into a viewer. Every annotated site residue of the chain that falls inside this unit, processing sites included -- for the main protease that is [1, 41, 145, 306], of which only 41 and 145 are the catalytic dyad and 1 and 306 are the cleavage boundaries of the chain itself. chemistry_only.anchors_in_the_fold is the shorter list.
how_to_read.reach.residues: ask 3's count -- how many residues a macrocycle sitting on those positions could reach, at 13.8 angstroms alpha carbon to alpha carbon, the anchors themselves included. A floor, never a ceiling.
how_to_read.reach.hydrophobic_and_reach.exposed: two counts over the same neighbourhood, not a conjunction, and neither is site_patch_positions. The residues that are both hydrophobic and exposed are the population a patch is drawn FROM; the patch itself is the largest connected component of them on the whole unit, so site_patch_positions is that component intersected with this neighbourhood and is routinely much shorter. On r02 nsp5, 11 residues here are both and 5 are in the patch; connectivity is the difference.
how_to_read.site_patch_positions: the residues of the unit's largest hydrophobic patch that lie inside this neighbourhood -- an intersection and not a search. Deliberately not a fresh patch search around the anchors: accessibility is a property of a residue in its surroundings, so re-growing components inside a 13.8-angstrom ball would report a surface assembled from faces the whole fold keeps buried. The cost is that a smaller patch sitting at the site is invisible here, so an empty list means the unit's largest patch is elsewhere, never that the site has no hydrophobic surface: nsp13's helicase C-terminal domain and nsp2's C-terminal domain both report nothing while each neighbourhood holds 3 residues that are both hydrophobic and exposed, 236.4 and 244.7 square angstroms of them.
how_to_read.site_patch_area_a2: ask 3's step 4 -- that intersection's area, so the patch stage 4 scored the unit on, measured only where it reaches this location. Comparable with another prediction and with nothing else.
how_to_read.site_patch_fraction_of_the_site: of everything a peptide at this site can touch, how much is patch. Denominator: the neighbourhood's own surface.
how_to_read.site_share_of_the_largest_patch: of the patch stage 4 scored this unit on, how much is at the chemistry. Denominator: the unit's largest patch. This is the number that says whether the surface score was earned where a binder would go.
how_to_read.chemistry_only: the reach and the site patch over the residues that do chemistry, with its own anchor_confidence; no unit_patch, which is a property of the whole unit and does not change. The subset is NOT a feature-type rule: a residue is dropped when its own description names a cleavage, so a plain Site can be kept -- Protein 3's `Involved in polymerization` is, and it is that chain's only annotated residue. same_as_the_full_set true means the subset is the whole set, and then reach, site_patch and anchor_confidence are null on purpose: the row's own figures are the answer and a copy could drift from them. Where it differs from the row, this is the one to read.

limitations: Every structure measured here is a prediction, and every row says so in its own `on_predicted_coordinates` and `is_deposited_measurement` -- read off `geometry.markers_from_coordinates` where a measurement was made rather than restated, so no row of this record can be pooled with a deposited one by a consumer that checks. ESMFold returns coordinates for any sequence it accepts, so a patch area at a site is an arithmetic on a model and not an observation of a protein. `anchor_confidence` is the only guide to whether the model committed to the residues the site was measured on, and it is the model's own opinion rather than an independent check.

The reach is alpha carbon to alpha carbon. `geometry._residues` keeps one atom per residue, so no side-chain coordinate exists to measure from: an extended lysine's terminal nitrogen sits about 6.4 angstroms out from its own alpha carbon, and two long side chains can therefore touch across a gap this counts as out of range. The neighbourhood is a floor on what a macrocycle at the site can contact and never a ceiling.

`reach.hydrophobic` and `reach.exposed` are two counts over the same neighbourhood and not a conjunction. The residues that are both -- which is the population a patch is drawn from -- are reported as `site_patch_positions`, restricted to the largest connected component, because that is the set the stage-4 arithmetic actually selects. The restriction is most of the difference rather than a detail: on the main protease 11 residues of the neighbourhood are both hydrophobic and exposed, covering 1,118.5 square angstroms, and 5 of them covering 586.7 are in the largest patch -- the other 6 belong to other components of the 18 that unit carries. So a smaller patch sitting at the site is invisible to `site_patch_area_a2`, and a zero there says the unit's largest patch is elsewhere and never that the site has no hydrophobic surface.

The reach itself is 13.8 angstroms, derived in `geometry` from the 600 square-angstrom footprint the scoring already assumes, and it inherits that footprint's roughness: 'roughly 400 to 800'. It is good to a couple of angstroms and not to a decimal place, so a residue count near the boundary should be read as approximate.

`PROCESSING_TERMS` is an authored term list, validated against no labelled corpus. It partitions a measurement into two that are both reported and it never drops a residue; the term that fired is recorded on every anchor so its effect is visible. Measured over this run, 28 of 29 plain `Site` residues name a cleavage.

A residue absent from this record is not a residue that does nothing. The annotation is bounded by what has been curated, and a novel pathogen's nearest relative is the least studied case by construction -- which is the case this pipeline exists for. Three chains here carry no annotated site residue at all.

A patch area measured on a prediction is comparable with another prediction and with nothing else. Checked on the one chain here that has a solved structure: anchored on the main protease's catalytic dyad, 6LU7 chain A gives 93 residues within reach against this prediction's 89, with 41 hydrophobic in both -- but a largest patch of 415.2 square angstroms over five residues against 2,012.6 over nineteen. The reach counts and the positions transfer; the areas do not.

An area off a low-confidence fold is inflated, and by how much is measurable here. The 18 units whose anchors average below pLDDT 70 have a mean exposed fraction of 0.793 and a mean largest patch of 3,608.5 square angstroms; the 5 at or above it have 0.611 and 1,592.4. A loosely predicted domain presents hydrophobic surface that a tightly packed one buries. What this does NOT touch is `site_share_of_the_largest_patch`, which is a ratio of two areas measured on the same coordinates: its Spearman correlation with the anchors' mean confidence over the 23 measured units is +0.21, which is no relationship worth reading. So a high share is not an artefact of a bad fold, and a large absolute area may well be.

`span_in_this_genome` and `positions_in_this_genome` are numbered along one open reading frame of this genome and not along the genome, so they are meaningless without the row's `reading_frame`. Two rows in different frames can carry spans that overlap as integers and share no residue: 26 pairs of the rows here do, spike S1's [24, 312] against the nucleoprotein's [41, 186] among them. Nothing may join, sort or plot on the span alone, and `orf_index` is a position in this run's 12-ORF pool rather than a frame identifier -- the strand, the codon offset and the nucleotide start beside it are the frame.

An anchor whose residue differs from the relative's is a substitution the alignment found, not a mapping error. The site is then conserved in position and not in identity, which is a weaker claim than the row's figures alone suggest.

A domain folded alone has lost whatever its neighbours contributed to its shape, and the neighbourhood is drawn only from residues inside the unit that was folded. A residue of the adjacent domain eleven angstroms from an active site is in contact with a macrocycle bound there and is not counted here, because these coordinates do not contain it.
